  Cross-cutting

  Storage abstraction: object storage behind a minimal interface with an S3/MinIO implementation and a plain-directory implementation — a deliberate hedge that keeps the service fully
  functional without cloud object storage approval.

  Observability: allow-list structured logging — stable event names plus explicitly-safe fields; exception messages and locals are never serialized (class and traceback locations only),
  because the payload domain is legal text and paid credentials. Request-correlation ids link background pipeline work back to the originating upload, and OpenTelemetry continues the
  caller's trace through this service into its dependencies. It fails open in every direction.

  Evaluation: two reproducible mini-benchmarks (judgments and legislation) with hash-pinned suites, planted negatives, and a held-out floor-calibration experiment, reporting Recall@1/3/6,
  MRR, nDCG, latency and vector footprint. Notably, the benchmark's own conclusion is not to switch models: GTE Large won on the primary metric by a single query, which the write-up
  explicitly rules insufficient, and Qwen 4B won on precision metrics while encoding ~289× slower on CPU. The production release gate is stated as an independently authored AoR-judged qrel
  set over the real ingested corpus and full hybrid path — the encoder benchmarks are explicitly not that.
